description: The exact index URLs for several NBRM instrument families (супервизорски циркулари/известувања до банките, decisions on accounting & financial reporting, methodology/rulebook annexes) were not individually confirmed — only individual act pages were seen.
Pre-adoption visibility for NBRM bylaws is unconfirmed; ENER coverage of central-bank secondary acts (as opposed to ministry laws) was not verified.
Albanian-language publication by NBRM was not investigated in this pass, despite Albanian being an official language in North Macedonia.
Historical archive depth of NBRM decisions (whether superseded versions remain retrievable) is unknown; consolidated 'пречистен текст' PDFs appear to be overwritten in place.
No confirmed way to search the Official Gazette by issuing authority ('Народна банка') was found, which would let A3 catch NBRM acts the bank's own site is slow to post.
The entire nbrm.mk source family — the cell's centre of gravity — is unreachable by the tooling available in this run (403 WAF).

The ENER browse/listing and search routes were not captured — only individual item-detail URLs are known. Without the listing route we cannot enumerate open consultations or read comment deadlines systematically.

Adjacent MK financial regulators that also consult on drafts were out of this cell's scope and were not scouted: Комисија за хартии од вредност (SEC), Агенција за супервизија на осигурување (ASO), МАПАС (pensions), Управа за финансиско разузнавање (FIU/AML), Комисија за заштита на конкуренцијата (interchange/competition).
No official NBRM RSS/Atom feed, e-mail alert list, or open-data/API endpoint for regulation was identified, and no NBRM Official-Gazette-linked machine-readable register was found.

No archival/backfill strategy was established for withdrawn or superseded drafts; NBRM republishes consolidated texts in place ('пречистен текст'), so prior versions and their transition deadlines silently disappear.
Albanian-language coverage was not attempted, although Albanian is an official language in North Macedonia and some government consultation material is issued bilingually.
Commercial regulatory-tracker vendors with confirmed North Macedonia coverage remain unidentified.

Local Skopje-based firms' own newsletters (e.g. Debarliev Dameski & Kelesoska, Polenak, Mens Legis, Lalicic & Partners, ODI Skopje) were only partially probed; their direct subscription feeds are likely faster than the aggregators that republish them.
No confirmed recent FSAP means periodic deep supervisory assessment coverage for MK is thin between annual EC reports.
No Macedonian-language legal-bulletin or consultancy-tracker service was located within this cell's scope.
Consultations specifically — English aggregators report adopted laws and application dates well, but rarely open consultation windows or draft-law comment periods.

State-owned and para-state entities that are heavy payments/cash consumers were not individually scouted: Македонска пошта (postal payments/counters), Фонд за ПИОМ (pension payouts), Агенција за вработување, ЕВН/state utilities, Централен регистар, and municipal treasuries.
No CPV code list was fixed for this cell, so neither the TED nor the ESJN collector has a precise filter yet.
IFI coverage is partial: EBRD, World Bank and EU/IPA were scouted, but EIB, Council of Europe Development Bank, UNDP/UNOPS MK procurement, KfW, USAID successors and Swiss SECO channels were not.
Albanian-language (sq) procurement publication was not searched at all; MK publishes some official content bilingually.
Several candidate URLs are inferred entry points (TED search page, ECEPP notice list, dkzjn.gov.mk root, data.gov.mk dataset filters) rather than pages fetched and confirmed in this pass.

Foreign parent-group IT suppliers of MK bank subsidiaries (NLB Group for NLB Banka, OTP for Ohridska/Sparkasse successor entities, Halkbank TR, Ziraat TR, ProCredit Holding, Steiermärkische/Sparkasse) were not searched. Group-level vendor announcements often cover the MK subsidiary implicitly.

Vendor job advertisements and bank IT job ads (which name the exact platform being implemented and the deadline) were not searched; nor were conference agendas and speaker lists (MBA events, MicroBalkans, KIBS/NBRM conferences).
Albanian-language (sq) sources were not covered at all in this cell.
MK company/contract registries (Central Registry crm.com.mk) were not queried to link vendor legal entities to bank-related activity or to identify newly incorporated vendor subsidiaries.

Card-scheme and infrastructure-side sources (Mastercard/Visa regional press, EBA CLEARING / ECB TIPS Western Balkans roll-out communications) were only glimpsed via one ECB item and not systematically mapped, although they announce MK participation and deadlines.

Non-bank PSPs, e-money institutions and payment institutions licensed under the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems were not individually enumerated; their career pages and training activity are unmapped.
Recruitment agencies and outsourced compliance-staffing providers operating in Skopje (a common route for niche regulatory-reporting roles) were not searched.
Job ads on MK boards are removed at the application deadline, so no historical series of posting volumes exists unless snapshots are taken.
Albanian-language coverage of vacancies, seminars and certification announcements is absent.
The highest-signal training agendas (MBA member seminars, in-house bank academies, vendor-run workshops) appear to be distributed privately rather than published.

Only the 2022 edition of the NBRM 'Извештај за поплаките примени во банките и штедилниците' was surfaced by search. The full back-series and the most recent editions (2023-2025) were not located, and the canonical index page that lists them was 403-blocked.

No specific Administrative, Higher Administrative, Supreme or Constitutional Court judgment concerning banking or payment-services fees was actually identified in this slice — only the registers where such judgments would live, plus generic Constitutional Court case permalinks whose subject matter was not confirmed.

The only confirmed State Audit Office audit of the National Bank found is the 2015 regularity audit. Whether DZR has since audited the NBRM's supervisory function, or audited it on a performance (not merely regularity) basis, is unestablished.

The Ministry of Finance's role as supervisor of financial companies (fast loans, leasing) — flagged by ОПМ as the complaint destination for that segment — was not itself scouted, nor was the Insurance Supervision Agency. Both sit adjacent to this cell's payments/banking scope.

Провизии.мк appears to be a bank-fee comparison portal but its operator, legal basis (whether it discharges a statutory fee-transparency obligation under the payment services law), and terms of use are unknown.
No Albanian-language (sq) searching was performed, per run scope. Regional consumer organisations and bilingual institutional output in Albanian remain uncovered.
No measurement of how well the Wayback Machine actually captures nbrm.mk .nspx pages and linked PDFs (snapshot frequency, whether PDFs are archived at all).
No systematic probe was possible for feed endpoints on the .gov.mk CMS estate (Umbraco-style ministries) or the .nspx sites — /feed, /rss, /wp-json, sitemap.xml were not tested.

Securities and Exchange Commission (Комисија за хартии од вредност), MAPAS (Агенција за супервизија на капитално финансирано пензиско осигурување), the Deposit Insurance Fund (Фонд за осигурување на депозити), the Macedonian Stock Exchange (МСЕ), the Central Registry (Централен регистар) and KIBS/clearing infrastructure were identified as relevant actors but no candidate URL was verified for them in this run.

The cell brief explicitly includes web-archive snapshots of BANK pages (tariffs, T&Cs, general conditions), but no individual commercial bank domain (Komercijalna, Stopanska, NLB, Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse, UNIBanka, Silk Road Bank etc.) was enumerated or archive-checked in this run.

Albanian-language coverage was not attempted. Albanian is an official language in North Macedonia and some government/consultation material is published in Albanian, but the run scope specified only mk and en.
The NBStat PxWeb API base path and version were inferred from standard PxWeb conventions rather than read off a documented endpoint; the portal root page showed no API link.
The exact index/search URLs inside slvesnik.com.mk for browsing issues by number and year, and for the free-access acts database, were not resolved because the site could not be fetched.
Individual committee pages for Комисија за финансирање и буџет and Комисија за економски прашања were not resolved to concrete URLs, only the committee index.

Searching was done in Macedonian and English only. Albanian is an official language in RNM and gazette/parliament material is published in Albanian too; no Albanian-language search was run and no Albanian glossary (ligj, projektligj, Fletorja Zyrtare, Kuvendi) was exercised.
No source was found that publishes transition/entry-into-force deadlines as structured data; they exist only as prose in преодни и завршни одредби of each statute.

The full amendment chronology for the core statutes (Закон за банките, Закон за платежни услуги и платни системи, ЗСППФТ, Закон за девизното работење) was only partially observed — individual gazette issues surfaced (90/2022, 208/2024, 37/2025, and a consolidated PSPS text versioned 267-25) but no complete chain was assembled.
Licence and API terms for AKADEMIKA and for the Службен весник publisher's subscription database were not established; both are behind registration.

No confirmed URL for the KZK concentration-notification listing/decision archive; the notification about ALTA GROUP acquiring control over Stopanska banka Bitola was visible only as a search snippet, and the site uses year-archive paths of unclear structure.
The UJP register of approved fiscal systems and its type-approval decisions were not located.
Albanian-language (sq) versions of these authorities' sites were not explored, although MK authorities publish bilingually (e.g. ASO's bilingual naming 'Agjencia e Mbikëqyrjes së Sigurimeve').
No RSS/Atom or structured API endpoint was identified for any of the six authorities; all candidates are currently HTML/PDF scrape targets.

Adjacent non-central-bank bodies that also impose payments-relevant obligations were not covered in this cell: Агенција за електронски комуникации (АЕК), Агенција за пошти (postal payment services), and Државен завод за ревизија. AEK and AP surfaced incidentally in searches.

Several candidate URLs were taken from search-result metadata rather than direct fetch (KZK, SEC, ASO category pages, ENER deep links, slvesnik sections); some kzk.gov.mk links are http-only and percent-encoded Cyrillic slugs that may be unstable.
ESMA and EIOPA equivalents of the EBA equivalence/cooperation work for North Macedonia (securities market and insurance supervision) were not searched in this pass.

Council of the EU documents — enlargement conclusions, Stabilisation and Association Council/Committee and the SAA sub-committee on internal market and competition (which handles financial services) — were not retrieved.
Albanian-language coverage was not attempted, although Albanian is an official language in North Macedonia and some institutional publications appear in it.

IPA III programming documents and the annual action programmes for North Macedonia (which fund and schedule financial-sector alignment work) were identified only indirectly through CFCD and the EU Delegation.
No URL in this slice was fetched or confirmed reachable; all entries rest on search-result metadata.
Operator rulebooks are likely participant-restricted (KIBS instant-payments scheme rules, CaSys card-system operating rules); only the MIPS rulebook is clearly public and versioned.
No source found yet for the domestic instant-payments scheme's own rulebook and its participant migration calendar (KIBS instant payments), nor for the TIPS Clone national implementation plan for MK.

Albanian-language coverage was not attempted (Albanian is an official language in North Macedonia and some regulator content is published in it), and English-language MK operator pages were not systematically enumerated.
No archival/versioning source was identified for superseded operator rulebooks other than the NBRSM MIPS versions page; historical KIBS/CaSys rule states may be unrecoverable.
Consultation and comment-period signals for payment-infrastructure rule changes are essentially absent from the sources found.
Agents and distributors of payment institutions / EMIs (агенти и дистрибутери) — PSD2-style registers usually list these separately, but no such MK sub-register was located.
Passporting / EEA-inbound and foreign bank branch listings were not located; unclear whether NBRNM publishes branches of foreign banks separately from domestic banks.
No archived/historical versions of any register were found, so licence grants and revocations cannot currently be dated from the registers themselves.
Службен весник на РСМ (Official Gazette) was not directly located as a searchable source in this pass, though licence decisions are published there.
Albanian-language (sq) register versions were not searched; a significant share of MK public-sector content is also published in Albanian.
Halkbank and Centralna kooperativna banka lack a confirmed dated notice channel; Silk Road's channel is a query-string CMS with no confirmed feed.

The full licensed-bank and savings-house universe was not enumerated in this pass; the cell brief's ten-bank list may omit smaller institutions and savings houses (штедилници) that also publish terms amendments.

The MK Pillar-3 artefact ('Извештај и податоци за Банката', per the NBRSM decision on disclosure of data and information) was confirmed only for TTK and partially for Stopanska and CCB; per-bank canonical URLs for the remaining banks are unmapped.
SEI-NET's search/listing mechanics (how to enumerate announcements by issuer and date, whether an open listing endpoint exists) were not established; only opaque document/file IDs were observed.

The 'consultations' topic is thinly served by this cell: banks respond to consultations mainly through the banking association rather than individually, and no association consultation-response publications were located.

Merchant/retail lobbying on card acceptance costs, interchange and POS/fiscalisation obligations was found only via the Chamber's Trade Association; no independent retailers' federation or card-acceptance interest group was identified.
Actual submitted consultation comments from associations (as opposed to news mentions that comments were submitted) were not located.
MASIT and Chamber member directories were only sampled (KIBS, CaSys) rather than fully enumerated; the full vendor/member ecosystem is unmapped.

Association LinkedIn/Facebook pages surfaced repeatedly (MBA-adjacent, ecommerce.mk, FIC, Union of Chambers) and often carry position announcements before the websites do, but social channels were not systematically catalogued.
No archival strategy was established for association content; chamber PDFs (annual reports back to 2007/2010) exist but position documents on specific drafts appear ephemeral.

This cell is scoped to Macedonian-language press, so Albanian-language business/financial media in North Macedonia (e.g. Portalb.mk, Koha, Albanian-language desks) is entirely uncovered, despite a substantial Albanian-speaking banking customer base and Albanian-language reporting on financial regulation.

No broadcast or video sources captured — governor and deputy-governor interviews frequently air on TV (Telma, Kanal 5, Alsat, MRT) and on podcast/YouTube formats, where regulatory intent is stated more freely than in print.

Journalists' and bank executives' personal social channels (LinkedIn, X) and the Macedonian Banking Association (МБА) communications were not mapped; association reactions to draft rules often precede press coverage.
No archival strategy identified for MK press; several outlets rotate or restructure URLs, and this run relied on live search only.
